Question Choices: A 10 by 10 grid has 100 small squares. If you shade 35 squares, what percent of the grid is shaded? Include the percent sign (%) in your answer.
Hints: A hundred-square grid represents 100%; each equal square represents 1%.
Solution: Each of 100 equal squares is 1%of the reference grid. 35 shaded squares represent 35/100=35%.

Question Choices: A square is divided into 100 equal parts. How many small squares should be shaded to show 57%?
Hints: A hundred-square grid represents 100%; each equal square represents 1%.
Solution: 57%means 57 out of 100. Shade 57 of the 100 equal squares.

Question Choices: Treat one complete shape or grid as 100%. Each grid is 10 by 10, with 100 equal squares. A student shaded one whole grid and then 9 more small squares on a second grid. What percent is shaded in total? Include the percent sign (%) in your answer.
Hints: Identify one reference whole as 100%. Add full wholes and fractional parts relative to that same whole.
Solution: One reference whole is 100%. Full wholes contribute 1×100%=100%. Extra fraction=9/100=9%. Total=100%+9%=109%of one whole.

Hints: Divide the part by the whole, then multiply by 100%.
